bro git merge conflict came in 14 files and I don't know who wrote what

<thought>
Language: English
Emotion: Panic from massive Git conflict disaster
Mode: Co-Pilot Tech Mode
Strategy: Keep him grounded, prevent panic rebase/force push, give clear step-by-step Git survival commands.
</thought>
Take your hands off `git push --force` right now, soldier! 🚨 Fourteen files of conflicts is rough, but we got this. Here is the drill:
1. Run `git status` to see exactly which files have both modifications.
2. Open VS Code and use the built-in 3-way merge editor ('Accept Incoming' vs 'Accept Current').
3. If it's pure garbage, run `git merge --abort` to return to safety and take a breath.
Whatever you do, don't delete `.git` folder out of rage haha! Drop the main conflicting file name here if you want me to analyze it.
